Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE OPINION NO. J2J S. MS. LENIE R. BAUTISTA MCGOO Municipality of Santa Cruz Province of Laguna CALABARZON Region Dear Madame: 2010 This pertains to your letterquery seeking legal opinion from this Department on whether or not an Acting Municipal Mayor has the authority to sign a Resolution approving the Supplemental Budget which was enacted in a session conducted by him as the Presiding Officer. In reply thereto, please be informed that your query has already been sufficiently addressed in DILG Opinion No. 11 series of 2008. In said opinion, we opined that the Vice Governor, as Acting Governor, exercises all the powers and perform all the duties and functions of the Governor except the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees. The signing of the Resolution by the Acting Municipal Mayor, not one of the limitations on the powers of the Acting Municipal Mayor, is sanctioned by law. For your ready reference, please find the attached copy of the aforesaid-DILG Opinion. Thank you and warm regards. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: . JESU DO Dir c r Ill /rb#28

ABES Provincial Administrator Provincial Capitol Building Patayan City, Nueva Ecija Dear Atty. Abesamis: This pertains to your equest for legal opinion with regard to the legality of the actions made y Vice Governor Edward Thomas L Joson, in his capacity as Acting G vernor, during the temporary absence of Governor Aurelio M. Umali. You represented that n 14 March 2008, Vice Governor Joson, as Acting Governor, issued se rall memoranda (l\/lemorandum Nos. 02-21, s. 2008) which, according to y 'u, effectively appoints or suspends essential personnel of the Provincial overnment, in contravention of the limitations provided fgr under Section 4 of the Local Government Code. A reading of the ser es of memorandum would reveal that Vice Governor Joson, as actin governor, directed certain officials and employees of the Provinci I Government to assume and perform the functions of certain offices, hich effectively replaced the officials earlier assigned by Governor Um Ii to perform the functions of the offices concerned. Hence, your que Section 46 (a) off the L cal Government Code provides: "(a) When th governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong barang , is temporarily incapacitated to perform the duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not Zimited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice governor, city or municipal vice mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member, shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to gppoinC, suspend, or dismiss employees, which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceed thirty (30) uyorking days. " (underlining ours) From the aforequoled provision oi the Local Government Code, it is clear that the Vice Governor, as Acting Governor due to the temporary

-2- incapacity of the Governor, shall automatically exercise all the powers and perform all the duties and functions of the Governor except the power to appoint, suspend or dismiss employees, which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds 30 working days- From the tenor of the several memoranda issued by the Acting Governor, it is clear that he directed certain officials and employees of the Provincial Government to perform the functions of certain offices thereat. Appointment is defined as "the selection, by the authority vested With the power, of an individual u,'ho is to perform the functions Of a given office" (Outline Review in Political Law Review by Antonio B. Nachura, p. 432). In the case of Borromeo vs. Mariano (41 Phil. 322), appointment was also defined as "the act of designation by the executive officer, board, or body to whom that power has been delegated, of thc individua! who is to exercise the functions of a given office". With the definition given on "appointment", we are of the view that the series of memoranda issued by Acting Governor Joson could well fall within the meaning and contemplation of the vvord "'appoint" found in Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code since it directed certain officials other than those officials earlier designated by Governor Umali to perform the functions of certain offices- Such being the case and per the 'imitations on the powers of the Acting Governor under Section 46 (a) of the Local Government Code, the subject series of memoranda should have only been issued by the Acting Governor at a time when the temporary incapacity of the Governor shall have already exceeded thirty (30) working days. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, A.
